name: Ukraine
summary: Ukraine is listed on the official registers as "Ukraine". This dossier records its status under five heritage-protection and international criminal law instruments, as shown on the UNESCO and United Nations Treaty Collection registers on 8 October 2026.

treaty_memberships.note: Signed 20 Jan 2000. The UN Treaty Collection page records a declaration by Ukraine under Article 124 stating that for seven years after the entry into force of the Statute for Ukraine it will not accept the Court's jurisdiction over crimes referred to in Article 8 (as amended) when it is likely that the crime was committed by its nationals; see the declarations section of the source page for the exact text. Entry-into-force date for Ukraine not read in this draft.

changelog.change: Initial draft rebuilt from the official registers, read in the built-in browser on 2026-10-08: UN Treaty Collection (Rome Statute, status as at 08-10-2026), UNESCO World Heritage States Parties page (page states as-of 22-Oct-2024), and UNESCO Legal Affairs pages for the 1954 Convention, First Protocol and Second Protocol. Dates are as shown on those pages; entry-into-force dates were not read. The earlier agent-written draft was empty because the registries were blocked in the cloud workspace. Not assessed: whether older dates were deposited under a predecessor state or earlier name (the registers list the current country name). Page-footnote texts on the UN Treaty Collection page were read only partly. region and summary are editorial labels, not taken from a source.

Verified all five treaty rows / not_party claims against the re-opened registers (UNESCO Legal Affairs 1954 Convention, First Protocol, Second Protocol; WHC States Parties list, page as-of 22-Oct-2024; UNTC Rome Statute status as at 08-10-2026): status, instrument type, dates and signatory notes match. Wording fixes: Rome Statute note: reworded Article 124 declaration to follow the UNTC text (will not accept jurisdiction over Article 8 crimes likely committed by its nationals) instead of the looser "acceptance ... war crimes alleged" paraphrase.
